correctness.rationale: After normalizing the endpoints to zero and one, conditioning on whether the observation is an endpoint contributes exactly \(p_1p_m/(p_1+p_m)\) to total variance; equality forces all interior mass to one point. For the upper side, the centered variable is a positive gap combination of cumulative-cut indicators and the gaps sum to one, so the \(L^2\) triangle inequality gives the maximum cut variance, strictly for at least two positive gaps. Explicit coalescing supports reach both limits and connectedness fills the interval. Fresh exact-rational replay verified the inequalities on 1800 generated profiles/supports.

value.rationale: This is the exact arbitrary-weight refinement of two classical complementary range/variance bounds. It quantifies precisely how known category frequencies sharpen both sides, identifies the active support geometries, and recovers the familiar equal-weight lower constant as a special case. That is a natural structural statistic with plausible reuse in finite-population and categorical dispersion work.
residual_risks: Older weighted finite-population or weighted range-variance literature may contain an equivalent theorem under another notation.

final_claim: For a finite law with a fixed positive ordered mass profile, \(\sigma^2/R^2\) has exact lower constant \(p_1p_m/(p_1+p_m)\) and upper constant \(\max_jP_j(1-P_j)\), with equality only in the stated two- and three-point cases, sharp boundary collapse for larger supports, and complete interval filling.
limitations: Finite positive atom profiles only, with support positions varying and range used as the normalization.
Most sharp endpoints for at least four atoms are boundary limits rather than attained strict supports.
